title: Sparse Minimality of Gaussian-Moments Counterexamples in Dimension Three
summary: No Gaussian-moment counterexample has both total degree at most four and at most four nonzero monomials in a fixed Gaussian Witt frame; the three surviving coefficient families satisfy the all-order mixed conclusion.

verification.scope: Fresh exact rational replay of 59,535 supports, source-aware review of coverage and the three all-order families, fresh standalone source build and visual PDF inspection.
verification.limits: Degree <=4 and support <=4 are simultaneous bounds in Gaussian Witt coordinates. Does not establish global degree/Pareto minimality. Independent mathematical review and separate-implementation replay have not occurred. Isolated internal AI PDF reading is recorded separately.

next_steps: Obtain external review of the finite coefficient-torus coverage and all-order family arguments.
abstract: We prove that a polynomial in three real Gaussian variables with total degree at most four and at most four nonzero monomials in a fixed Gaussian Witt frame satisfies the mixed-moment conclusion whenever all its positive pure moments vanish. The proof combines an exhaustive exact calculation over 59,535 supports with all-order arguments for three surviving coefficient families: isotropic linear forms, polynomial Gaussian shears, and orthogonal products with an isotropic factor. Moment ideals through order twenty-four exclude every other active support. Together with Long’s five-term quartic counterexample, the result shows that five Witt-coordinate monomials are necessary and sufficient for a failure of degree at most four. The degree bound and the chosen notion of support are essential restrictions of the result.
